# Abstract

::: { .justify }

The automation of literature search execution is becoming increasingly important as publication volumes grow and AI-based, agentic systems augment academic search activities. However, some Application Programming Interfaces (APIs) lack support for academic search queries consisting of nested subqueries and Boolean operators. This constraint complicates systematic and reproducible searches, increases manual effort, and decreases search efficiency. To resolve this issue, we present the Query Emulation for Academic Literature Searches (QuEALS) technique, which allows researchers to conduct automated API-based searches with academic search queries even when APIs do not support them natively. This approach works by recursively processing the query, retrieving literature from the API, and filtering the results for subqueries. We followed a Design Science Research approach to design, implement, and evaluate QuEALS. The prototype was implemented and evaluated for Crossref, which offers one of the most comprehensive and open research APIs, but lacks support for academic search queries.

:::
